headline: Flyers place Rasmus Ristolainen on IR, activate Cam York
take:
Daily Faceoff reports the Flyers have placed Rasmus Ristolainen on injured reserve and activated Cam York, who had been out close to three weeks with an upper-body injury. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor posted that York "basically will just replace Ristolainen in the lineup."

The Flyers are 3-7-4 and their numbers say it isn't just bad luck. They have 42% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) so far this season, and that drops to 40% at five-on-five. Both defensemen have been on the wrong side of that: with York on the ice, the team's expected-goal share is 6.68 points worse than without him, and with Ristolainen it's 11.3 points worse, in small samples of six and four games. Ristolainen has one goal on 0.33 expected, so his results have run ahead of his chances. York has none on 0.7 expected, so his are running behind. Neither swap changes the team's strength much.

The real change is who absorbs the minutes. In the one game since Ristolainen went out, Jamie Drysdale moved in beside Sanheim and jumped to 26:48 a night from 20:02, while Hunter McDonald rose to 13:08 from 8:42. That's based on games already played without him, and with York back, expect Drysdale's workload to ease.
